column3: Near-verbatim parallel: enduring righteous deeds are better with the Lord in reward and outcome.
Contrasts guidance with manifest error and names the final return, supporting the focus's true outcome.
Directly states that God increases those who are guided in guidance.
God's better reward and better outcome closely parallel the focus's final valuation.
The immediate context presents unbelievers' boast about superior worldly standing, answered by 19:76.
Withheld guidance after knowing rejection is a negative counterpart to increased guidance.
God increases believing righteous doers from His bounty, closely matching the focus's growth and deeds.
The immediately preceding verse sets the misguided persons' apparent extension against 19:76.
Faith and righteous deeds lead to divine guidance, supplying the focus's moral pattern.
The garden owner's claim of a better return contrasts with the focus's true better outcome.
The survivors remaining after the flood do not clarify enduring righteous deeds.
Increasing disbelief is the inverse trajectory to God's increase of the guided.
God increases the goodness of a good deed, directly reinforcing righteous deeds as enduring gain.
The preceding verse exposes the destruction of people with superior worldly adornment.
Ritual purification of clothing does not materially develop the focus.
What is with God is better and more lasting than worldly enjoyment, directly echoing the focus.
Creation from nothing does not clarify guidance growth or enduring deeds.
God grants good doers reward in this life and the Hereafter, directly supporting the focus's reward.
God's reward is better for believers who do righteous deeds, with patience sustaining that judgment.
Turning back after divine guidance provides the negative counterpart to remaining and growing guided.
God is better and more enduring than Pharaoh, reinforcing the focus's measure of lasting good.
Faith and righteous deeds identify the best of creation, supporting the focus's valuation of such deeds.
The announcement of Yahya does not clarify the focus's guidance and reward theme.
The warning against being turned back from faith is a distant negative counterpart to increased guidance.
What is with God is better for the righteous and includes abiding gardens.
Return to God for judgment loosely relates to the focus's better final return.
Obedience that turns believers back and makes them losers contrasts with continuing guidance.
Believing righteous doers receive full reward and additional divine bounty.
The identification of Jesus does not develop the focus's theme.
The more severe and lasting afterlife punishment contrasts with the focus's better lasting outcome.
Only the Lord endures, providing a theological ground for valuing what remains.
Divine mastery and death's attendants do not clarify the focus's specific relation.
God's continuing guidance and restoration of the righteous parallel guidance as an ongoing divine gift.
God does not lose righteous labor and grants the best reward from Himself.
The promised birth of a pure son does not clarify the focus.
Repeated rejection and increased disbelief contrast with the focus's increase in guidance.
God's recompense is better for those who believe and are mindful of Him.
Moses's return to his mother is unrelated to enduring deeds or guided growth.
Guidance and glad tidings for believers offer only a general thematic link.
Faith is identified as being guided, contrasting belief with divisive turning away.
God's creative command does not clarify the focus's reward theme.
An encounter can increase aversion rather than guidance, forming a clear negative contrast.
Submission to God is identified with being guided, giving the focus's basic orientation.
The gift of scripture and prohibition on supporting deniers do not directly develop the focus.
Questioning resurrection does not clarify enduring righteous deeds.
Good sent ahead is found with God as better and greater in reward.
Jesus's prayer and almsgiving command gives concrete examples of righteous deeds in the same surah.
Faith and righteous deeds are the exception to human loss, broadly supporting enduring works.
The Lord's provision is better and more lasting than worldly display.
Secret cooperation with opponents of revelation does not directly clarify the focus.
The refusal of forgiveness is linked to a people whom God does not guide, a distant negative counterpart.
God increased believing youths in guidance, using the focus's exact formulation.
Moses continues the same favored-prophet sequence but has no direct guidance-and-reward link.
Worse recompense, place, and straying form a punitive contrast to the focus's better outcome.
The Prophet is upon straight guidance, a general positive instance of the focus's condition.
Pharaoh's wife's protection of Moses does not clarify the focus.
Return to God and the fate of excesses loosely relates to final outcomes.
The destruction of Thamud does not illuminate enduring righteous deeds.
Zechariah's creation from nothing does not develop the focus's theme.
Revelation can increase rebellion and disbelief, contrasting with increase in guidance.
Return to the Lord for punishment is only a broad final-outcome parallel.
Moses's return to his mother is unrelated to the focus.
The distinction between guided and transgressing descendants gives only a broad contrast.
Being reduced to the lowest state is a remote contrast to growth in guidance.
Prayer, almsgiving, and being pleasing to the Lord concretely exemplify enduring righteous deeds.
The demand for more worldly increase contrasts only loosely with divine increase in guidance.
God extends provision to both parties, paralleling 19:75's extension without affirming their final worth.
Rejecting guidance after it becomes clear is a negative counterpart to increased guidance.
God holds reward for both this world and the Hereafter, correcting a narrowed reward horizon.
Believing righteous doers receive blessedness and a good final return.
God rewards truthful believers with abiding gardens as the recompense of good doers.
God's freely given favor offers a general basis for the focus's divine increase.
A plan to commit wrong before becoming righteous contrasts with genuinely enduring righteous deeds.
God guides those who discern and follow the best message.
What is with God is better and more lasting than worldly enjoyment.
A great reward from God is a direct but general counterpart to the focus's reward.
The image of covering oneself does not materially develop the focus.
Disbelief increases only wrath and loss, a direct negative contrast to increasing guidance.
Believers unmixing faith with wrongdoing are secure and guided.
What remains with God is better for believers, closely echoing the focus's enduring good.
An irreversible punishment decree does not clarify the focus.
Marked punishment for excesses does not materially develop the focus.
Repentance joined to righteous action becomes a true return to God.
Believing righteous worshippers have their reward with their Lord and no fear or grief.
Salih's call to mindfulness does not directly clarify the focus.
What is better with the Lord is enduring garden reward and divine pleasure for the mindful.
God guides whom He wills, supplying the source of the focus's increased guidance.
God's exclusive guidance and favor are broadly related to His granting increase.
The Quran guides to what is most upright and promises a great reward to righteous believers.
Believers can increase in faith while the same sign exposes others to misguidance.
Degrees, forgiveness, and mercy give only a general picture of divine reward.
Following guides who seek no wage is only indirectly related to being guided.
The location at the lote tree does not clarify the focus.
Those who strive for God are guided to His ways, joined to His presence with good doers.
The final settling-place is with the Lord, supporting the focus's concern with ultimate return.
Persistent corruption without reform is a broad contrast to righteous deeds.
The possibility of much good in a disliked matter is too general to clarify the focus.
Rejecting the messengers' clear signs is a distant negative counterpart to guidance.
Mindfulness of God and obedience to the messenger broadly support the guided path.
Their opportunistic claim of guidance contrasts with the stable growth in guidance of the focus.
Hearing God's verses increases believers in faith, a close parallel to increased guidance.
Revelation increases believers in faith, directly extending the focus's growth-in-guidance theme.
Revelation increasing the diseased in defilement forms the inverse of God increasing the guided.
Every effort in God's path is recorded as a righteous deed for the best recompense.
Small and great expenditures and journeys are recorded so God may reward the best of deeds.
Those who do good receive the best reward and more, directly complementing the focus's better reward.
Believers who do righteous deeds and humble themselves to their Lord are enduring companions of the Garden.
God commands patience and does not let the reward of good doers be lost.
God does not let the reward of good doers be lost.
God does not let the reward of those who are mindful and patient be lost.
Steadfast worship, charity, and repelling evil culminate in the good final home.
The righteous enter enduring gardens, clarifying the lasting return of faithful deeds.
The greeting of peace for patient endurance names the excellent final home.
What people possess ends, while what is with God remains; the patient receive the best recompense.
Believing men and women who do righteousness receive a good life and the best recompense.
The Hereafter is better for those who do good, reinforcing the focus's superior outcome.
One who seeks the Hereafter, strives for it, and believes has an appreciated effort.
God does not let the reward of those who do good deeds be lost.
Faith and righteous action receive the best reward and an eased command.
The immediate continuation contrasts a denier's boast of future wealth and children with the focus's true lasting value.
God inherits the denier's claimed possessions, exposing their failure to endure against righteous deeds.
One who comes to the Lord believing and doing righteous deeds receives the highest degrees and abiding gardens.
A believing person's righteous effort is not denied and is recorded by God.
Believers who do righteous deeds enter gardens beneath which rivers flow.
Believers who do righteous deeds receive forgiveness and noble provision.
Repentance, faith, and righteous deeds are transformed by God into good deeds.
The patient receive lofty chambers and a lasting greeting of peace.
God removes the evils of believers who do righteous deeds and rewards them according to their best deeds.
The hidden joy prepared for faithful servants is a recompense for their deeds.
Good words rise to God and righteous deeds He raises, linking good works with enduring divine reception.
God gives full reward and increases servants from His bounty, closely paralleling the focus's divine increase.
The patient receive their reward without measure, supporting the focus's superior divine recompense.
God rewards believers according to the best of what they did.
Believers who do righteous deeds have an unfailing reward.
God accepts the best deeds of righteous believers and overlooks their evils among the companions of Paradise.
God sends tranquility into believers' hearts so that they increase in faith.
A good loan to God is multiplied and receives a generous reward.
Charitable believers receive multiplication and a generous reward.
Faithful striving is directed toward forgiveness and a vast garden, the lasting divine favor.
A good loan to God is multiplied and forgiven, directly joining increase with divine reward.
God removes evils and magnifies the reward of one who is mindful of Him.
The reward is explicitly tied to a servant's appreciated effort.
Believers who do righteous deeds have an unfailing reward.
The Hereafter is better and more enduring, directly expressing the focus's lasting-value criterion.
Success belongs to the one who purifies himself, a concrete righteous orientation toward the lasting good.
Believers who do righteous deeds have an unending reward.
The believers' righteous deeds culminate in their Lord's reward, abiding gardens, and mutual good pleasure.
Even the smallest good deed is seen, affirming the enduring accountability of righteous action.
God multiplies charitable spending manyfold, a clear example of divine increase for a righteous deed.
Those who give charitably have their reward with their Lord and no fear or grief.
God multiplies even an atom's weight of good and grants a great reward from Himself.
Believers who do righteous deeds enter Paradise without injustice, affirming the reliable final return.
God promises forgiveness and a great reward to believers who do righteous deeds.
Faith and righteous action are paired with freedom from fear and grief.
A good deed receives tenfold recompense, a concrete expression of divine increase in reward.
Believers who do righteous deeds are enduring companions of Paradise.
The mindful receive forgiveness and gardens, called an excellent reward for those who do good.
A threatening report increases believers in faith, directly paralleling faithful increase.
God gives believers who do righteous deeds their full rewards.
Secret charity, kindness, and reconciliation done for God bring a great reward.
Believers who do righteous deeds enter lasting gardens by God's true promise.
The guided have the abode of peace with their Lord as the final fruit of their deeds.
The patient who do righteous deeds receive forgiveness and a great reward.
Believers who do righteous deeds enter gardens abiding by their Lord's permission.
Those who do good receive good in this life, while the Hereafter is better.
Believers who do righteous deeds receive the gardens of Paradise as their lodging.
Believers who do righteous deeds enter gardens of lasting beauty and blessing.
The successful believers inherit Paradise and remain there eternally.
Faithful righteous action is promised secure establishment and worship of God.
Believers who do righteous deeds are delighted in a garden.
Believers who do righteous deeds receive gardens of bliss, abiding therein.
Faithful obedience and remembrance culminate in forgiveness and a great reward.
Believers who do righteous deeds receive forgiveness and noble provision.
Following the Reminder and fearing the Merciful brings forgiveness and a noble reward.
Believing righteous men and women enter Paradise and are provided without measure.
Believers who do righteous deeds are in garden meadows with whatever they desire from their Lord.
God admits believers who do righteous deeds into His mercy, the manifest success.
The most honored with God are the most mindful, clarifying the true measure of worth.
Believers and their faithful descendants are joined in Paradise without loss of any deed.
God strengthens believers with a spirit from Him and admits them to abiding gardens.
Patience is recompensed with a garden and fine clothing.
The righteous are in enduring bliss, a final-outcome counterpart to the focus.
Giving, mindfulness, and affirming the good define a path toward divinely eased goodness.
The most mindful person gives to purify himself, exemplifying a righteous deed oriented to God.
